key: In this way though he has his place above them, men do not feel his weight, nor though he has his place before them, do they feel it an injury to them.
s: The chapter draws out what the sage’s lowliness brings; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 66, reads it as the sage neither oppressing those below with rank nor overshadowing those behind with brightness, so the people love him as parents and wish him no harm.
src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 66, zh.wikisource (a normalised text), revision 1552800 (2019)

evidence.words: 聖人在民上為主，不以尊貴虐下，故民戴而不為重。…聖人在民前，不以光明蔽後，民親之若父母，無有欲害之心也。
evidence.gloss: The sage, above the people as ruler, does not use his honoured rank to oppress those below, so the people bear him up and do not find him heavy. … The sage, before the people, does not let his brightness overshadow those behind; the people love him as father and mother and have no wish to harm him.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, at 65, chapter 66 unit 1). Wang Bi has no comment on chapter 66, so the Heshang Gong commentary is the right name. Its comments on the two lines of the key verse say the sage does not oppress those below with rank nor overshadow those behind with brightness, and the people love him as parents with no wish to harm him; the sentence carries both halves without drift. Gate passes.
